system:
You decide what happens to each tested hypothesis next, from the evidence.

## Decisions

- `keep`: the claim stands as it is; it is carried forward without retesting.
- `refine`: the claim needs a changed clause, scope or mechanism; give the new `statement`. It is tested as a new hypothesis.
- `shelve`: set it aside. It can be revived later if the run stops making progress.

## How to decide

- A result that rests on one measurement of one artifact is weak evidence either way.
- Do not shelve a claim that wins on some part of the task, even if it loses overall: say so in `rationale`.
- Weigh what supports each claim against what refutes it, and cite those observation ids in `rationale`.
- Decide every hypothesis listed. Call submit_revision once.

system:
You open lines of investigation. You map where answers and evidence could lie, and propose hypotheses to test. Others build and test them; you do not judge them.

## The map

- Hypothesis regions: kinds of answer, grouped under axes (the dimensions answers differ along).
- Observation regions: kinds of evidence, grouped under axes (where and how one would look).
- Add a region only if it is distinct from every region already on the map. Add an axis only if it is new, or subsumes an existing axis (then set `replaces_axis`).
- Each map holds at most 10 regions. A region proposed to a full map is dropped, and a hypothesis naming a region that is not on the map is left unplaced; file it in an existing region instead.
- You can use the tools to look at the environment before you propose; a hypothesis grounded in what exists beats one about what might.

## Hypotheses

- Propose 3 hypotheses in the least explored regions and axes (counts are shown; UNTRIED regions and thin axes first). Each needs a testable `statement`, a `rationale`, and a `region`.
- Make them compete: different regions, different mechanisms, not variants of one idea.
- Read the evidence on last round's hypotheses and every hypothesis's metrics per part of the task. Do not re-propose what is held.
- If hypotheses win on different parts, or the best score has stopped improving, at least one proposal must be a combination (name the hypotheses and what it takes from each).
- Call submit_exploration once.

system:
You decide what happens to each tested hypothesis next, from the evidence.

## Decisions

- `keep`: the claim stands as it is; it is carried forward without retesting.
- `refine`: the claim needs a changed clause, scope or mechanism; give the new `statement`. It is tested as a new hypothesis.
- `shelve`: set it aside. It can be revived later if the run stops making progress.

## How to decide

- A result that rests on one measurement of one artifact is weak evidence either way.
- Do not shelve a claim that wins on some part of the task, even if it loses overall: say so in `rationale`.
- Weigh what supports each claim against what refutes it, and cite those observation ids in `rationale`.
- Decide every hypothesis listed. Call submit_revision once.

system:
You open lines of investigation. You map where answers and evidence could lie, and propose hypotheses to test. Others build and test them; you do not judge them.

## The map

- Hypothesis regions: kinds of answer, grouped under axes (the dimensions answers differ along).
- Observation regions: kinds of evidence, grouped under axes (where and how one would look).
- Add a region only if it is distinct from every region already on the map. Add an axis only if it is new, or subsumes an existing axis (then set `replaces_axis`).
- Each map holds at most 10 regions. A region proposed to a full map is dropped, and a hypothesis naming a region that is not on the map is left unplaced; file it in an existing region instead.
- You can use the tools to look at the environment before you propose; a hypothesis grounded in what exists beats one about what might.

## Hypotheses

- Propose 3 hypotheses in the least explored regions and axes (counts are shown; UNTRIED regions and thin axes first). Each needs a testable `statement`, a `rationale`, and a `region`.
- Make them compete: different regions, different mechanisms, not variants of one idea.
- Read the evidence on last round's hypotheses and every hypothesis's metrics per part of the task. Do not re-propose what is held.
- If hypotheses win on different parts, or the best score has stopped improving, at least one proposal must be a combination (name the hypotheses and what it takes from each) or a `revive` of an eligible shelved hypothesis.
- Call submit_exploration once.

h4.why: This is the earliest disease-linked item surfaced, so the pass does not establish an earlier family-based report.

h7.why: The earliest dissemination already uses PD/EOPD terminology rather than the rare-disease label.

h8.why: It shows the core disease association entering PubMed first as a preprint.

observations.content: A 2025 review, 'The genetics of autosomal recessive early-onset Parkinson's disease,' explicitly discusses AR EOPD genes and is a plausible synthesis paper that can place PSMF1 in that broader gene set.

h13.why: This supports the part of the hypothesis asserting that a secondary synthesis paper exists placing PSMF1 among emerging AR-EOPD genes.

observations.content: The retrieved literature does not yet include a PubMed-indexed synthesis that explicitly names the syndrome label CONDMCB or cleanly connects that label to PSMF1; the available synthesis is broader and phenotype-oriented (EOPD).

h13.why: This matches the hypothesis that the PubMed literature retrieved here lacks a concise genotype-first synthesis explicitly tying PSMF1 to CONDMCB.

observations.content: A 2025 preprint reports that PSMF1 variants cause a phenotypic spectrum from early-onset Parkinson's disease to perinatal lethality and disrupt mitochondrial function, indicating direct human genetic evidence for disease association.

h13.why: This is primary disease evidence, not the secondary synthesis the hypothesis is about.

observations.content: Functional follow-up papers on PI31/PSMF1 biology exist, including a mouse model paper and a study of an FBXO7 patient mutation affecting PI31/proteasomes/mitochondria.

h13.why: These papers strengthen the functional literature but do not provide the missing genotype-first synthesis tied to CONDMCB.

observations.content: PubMed indexing now shows multiple PSMF1/PI31-related reports under Parkinsonism/EOPD terminology, including a 2026 German Parkinson's disease cohort letter (42649079), a 2026 Nature Communications paper on a phenotypic spectrum from parkinsonism to perinatal lethality (41986367), a 2025 medRxiv preprint on early-onset Parkinson's disease to perinatal lethality (39148840), and a 2025 review of autosomal recessive early-onset Parkinson's disease (41253044).

h16.why: The literature is discoverable via broad PD/EOPD terms and includes cohort/review articles, not only syndrome-name searches.

observations.content: The 2026 Nat Commun paper is indexed with Humans and Parkinsonian Disorders/Parkinson Disease MeSH and its title explicitly links PSMF1 to parkinsonism; the 2025 preprint also states an EOPD-to-perinatal-lethality spectrum. No PubMed record found here used the rare disease label CONDMCB in title/abstract, and a direct PubMed query for CONDMCB or the full syndrome name returned zero hits.

h16.why: This supports the claim that the syndrome label itself is not the main retrieval hook in PubMed, whereas broader Parkinsonism terminology is.

observations.content: The 2026 Nat Commun study includes animal and cellular mechanistic work: MeSH terms include mice, Drosophila melanogaster, fibroblasts, mitochondrial membrane potential, and disease models, indicating functional follow-up after human gene discovery.

h16.why: Functional studies broaden the record beyond the rare-disease name and are recoverable with gene/proteostasis/PD queries.

observations.content: The 2025 review frames PSMF1 within autosomal recessive EOPD genetics, and the 2026 cohort letter explicitly centers on PSMF1 variants in a German PD cohort. This indicates that later literature is being organized under AR-EOPD/PD rather than under CONDMCB.

h16.why: The evidence aligns with the hypothesis that gene-focused PD/EOPD literature has a broader footprint than the rare syndrome name.

observations.content: The 2026 Nature Communications paper reports PSMF1 variants causing a phenotypic spectrum from parkinsonism to perinatal lethality and indexes humans, fibroblasts, mice, Drosophila, and mitochondria, directly linking disease variants to functional biology.

h15.why: This is the strongest direct support: the paper combines human genetics with mechanistic work in fibroblasts and model organisms and reports mitochondrial involvement.

observations.content: The 2025 medRxiv preprint is the same study as the 2026 Nature Communications article and already describes PSMF1 variants, early-onset Parkinson's disease, perinatal lethality, and mitochondrial dysfunction.

h15.why: It shows that the mechanistic and human-genetics package was present before journal publication.

observations.content: PI31/PSMF1 was previously studied as an adaptor for proteasome transport in axons and as required for synaptic development in a 2019 Developmental Cell paper.

h15.why: This provides earlier mechanistic biology relevant to proteasome regulation, even though it predates the disease paper.

observations.content: A 2025 PNAS paper reports PI31 expression is neuroprotective in a mouse model of early-onset parkinsonism and indexes mice, neurons, and Drosophila.

h15.why: This is additional functional evidence that PI31 biology affects parkinsonism-relevant neurodegeneration.

observations.content: The evidence found does not refute the claim that functional studies are central to interpreting PSMF1 disease variants; instead, the human disease paper itself is heavily mechanistic.

h15.why: No contradictory paper was identified in this pass; the retrieved literature consistently points toward functional biology plus human genetics.

observations.content: A broad review on proteasomes is not disease-specific and does not by itself establish the PSMF1 disease mechanism.

h15.why: Useful background only; it neither supports nor refutes the disease-gene claim.

observations.content: A PubMed-indexed review exists on autosomal recessive early-onset Parkinson's disease (PMID 41253044) and its abstract frames PSMF1 as part of the AR-EOPD gene landscape; however, the retrieved PubMed record does not use the syndrome label CONDMCB or explicitly bridge that label to PSMF1. A separate PSMF1 disease preprint (PMID 39148840) exists, but it is not a genotype-first synthesis and likewise does not establish a PubMed-indexed CONDMCB-linked review.

h17.why: This matches the hypothesis: a secondary synthesis paper exists, but the retrieved PubMed literature still lacks a concise genotype-first synthesis explicitly tying PSMF1 to the syndrome label CONDMCB.

observations.content: The retrieved literature includes a 2025 review on autosomal recessive EOPD and a 2025 preprint plus a 2026 cohort letter on PSMF1 variants in Parkinson's disease, showing that PSMF1 is being incorporated into gene-discovery/synthesis discussions. None of these retrieved PubMed items are indexed as a syndrome-specific synthesis using CONDMCB nomenclature.

h17.why: The evidence supports the broader synthesis component while not contradicting the absence of a CONDMCB-labeled genotype-first synthesis.

observations.content: The human disease literature is centered on one primary study: Magrinelli et al. first appeared as a medRxiv preprint (39148840) and then as a journal article in Nature Communications (41986367), both describing PSMF1 variants causing a phenotypic spectrum from early-onset Parkinson's disease/parkinsonism to perinatal lethality. A later letter, 'PSMF1 Variants in a German Parkinson's Disease Cohort' (42649079), appears to be cohort extension rather than an independent syndrome-defining family report.

h14.why: This fits the idea that the PSMF1 disease literature is anchored by a single core human-genetics report, with later papers mainly extending phenotype or adding cohort-level observations.

observations.content: The 2026 Nature Communications paper (41986367) has Humans/Parkinsonian Disorders/Parkinson Disease/Pedigree/Fibroblasts/Mice/Drosophila MeSH terms and directly reports the human disease link for PSMF1. The FEBS Journal paper on an FBXO7 patient mutation (38466799) is human and fibroblast-based but concerns FBXO7 rather than PSMF1 as the causal gene, so it is related mechanistically but does not establish the PSMF1 syndrome itself.

h14.why: Related human papers exist that mention PI31/PSMF1 biology but do not add new PSMF1 families, implying the literature is broader than the single core report alone.

observations.content: Functional follow-up papers are present after the human gene discovery: 41986367 includes animal and cellular models in the same article; 40956890 specifically studies PI31 expression as neuroprotective in a mouse model of early-onset parkinsonism; 38466799 examines FBXO7 patient mutation effects on Fbxo7/PI31 co-regulation of proteasomes and mitochondria; 26086101 is an earlier proteasome-biology paper on VCP and PSMF1 without the disease phenotype. These are follow-up/mechanistic rather than new human case series.

h14.why: Mechanistic studies broaden the literature set but do not directly determine whether there are additional independent case reports.

observations.content: A 2025 review on autosomal recessive early-onset Parkinson's disease (41253044) includes PSMF1 in a broader EOPD genetics framework. The 2026 German cohort letter (42649079) indicates PSMF1 is being tracked in PD cohorts rather than only as a single-family syndrome gene.

h14.why: This is consistent with later papers being synthesis/cohort literature rather than multiple independent syndrome-defining reports.

observations.content: Peer-reviewed indexed items retrieved here include the core Nature Communications report (41986367), a German PD cohort letter (42649079), an AR-EOPD review (41253044), and mechanistic studies (38466799, 26086101). The only paper among these that directly defines the PSMF1 disease entity is the Magrinelli Nature Communications article.

h14.why: The indexed peer-reviewed set looks small and centered on one foundational report plus follow-up literature.

observations.content: The preprint (39148840) is the earlier version of the same Magrinelli study later published in Nature Communications (41986367), not an independent additional human discovery paper.

h14.why: This supports the notion of a single core report rather than multiple separate discovery studies.

observations.content: The strongest functional modeling evidence comes from the Magrinelli paper itself, which includes fibroblast, mouse, and Drosophila work, and from later mouse/biochemistry studies (40956890, 38466799) that build on the same PI31/PSMF1 pathway.

h14.why: Later modeling papers extend mechanism downstream of the human finding instead of defining new patients.

observations.content: Among PSMF1/PI31 PubMed hits, only the Magrinelli report is a direct PSMF1 disease-defining paper; the rest are reviews, cohort/letter material, or mechanistic studies. The search also surfaces adjacent proteasome/PI31 papers that are not disease case reports.

h14.why: The literature landscape is dominated by one disease report plus follow-up studies, matching the hypothesis.

observations.content: The later Nature Communications paper (PMID 41986367) is a mechanistic follow-up by the same Magrinelli-led group; its MeSH terms include Humans, Mice, Fibroblasts, Drosophila melanogaster, Parkinsonian Disorders, and Parkinson Disease, indicating functional extension of the gene-disease link rather than a new independent discovery cohort.

h14.why: A same-group mechanistic follow-up fits the claim that later literature mainly extends the phenotype and biology after the core report.

observations.content: The German Parkinson's disease cohort letter (PMID 42649079) has no abstract and is indexed as a Letter, which fits a brief cohort/variant report in broader PD literature rather than a syndrome-defining case series.

h14.why: This is consistent with the literature being anchored by one core report and later brief cohort follow-up.

observations.content: The preprint (PMID 39148840) explicitly states that PSMF1 variants cause a phenotypic spectrum from early-onset Parkinson's disease to perinatal lethality and discusses disrupted mitochondrial function, showing that the human literature has expanded from the original childhood-onset syndrome to a broader spectrum.

h14.why: This supports a single foundational human-genetics paper with later spectrum-expanding work.

observations.content: PubMed searches for PSMF1 with parkinsonism/EOPD terms repeatedly return the Magrinelli paper first, followed by the German cohort letter and later mechanistic papers, with no clear second independent syndrome-defining family report emerging from the search results.

h14.why: The search pattern itself continues to point to one core report rather than multiple separate human case-report anchors.

observations.content: I did not retrieve any additional PubMed-indexed paper in this iteration that appears to present a distinct new family establishing the syndrome independently of the Magrinelli report; the new items were follow-up, preprint, or cohort/letter literature.

h14.why: This is evidence against the existence of multiple independent syndrome-defining human reports in PubMed.

h_regions.name: Human case reports
h_regions.description: Primary reports describing affected individuals/families with the PSMF1-related neurodevelopmental/parkinsonian phenotype.

h_regions.name: Functional modeling
h_regions.description: Cell, animal, or biochemical studies testing the pathogenicity/mechanism of disease-associated PSMF1 variants or PI31 deficiency.

h_regions.name: Secondary synthesis
h_regions.description: Reviews, cohort summaries, or disease-gene overviews that aggregate previously reported PSMF1 cases.

o_regions.name: Indexed PubMed reports
o_regions.description: PubMed-indexed case reports, letters, cohorts, and functional papers mentioning PSMF1, PI31, parkinsonism, or related phenotypes.

o_regions.description: Final journal articles and letters; excludes preprints unless they correspond to the same study later published.

o_regions.name: Preprints
o_regions.description: medRxiv/bioRxiv versions of the same work, useful for tracking the earliest description of the variant-disease relationship.

o_regions.name: Full-text disease report
o_regions.description: PubMed-indexed papers whose abstract or MeSH indicates they directly report patients/families with the PSMF1/PI31-associated neurodegenerative-parkinsonian phenotype, even if the syndrome name differs.

o_regions.name: Mechanistic follow-up
o_regions.description: PubMed-indexed functional studies that probe PSMF1/PI31 biology in fibroblasts, mice, flies, neurons, or biochemistry after the human disease link is established.

o_regions.name: Gene discovery synthesis
o_regions.description: PubMed-indexed reviews, cohort letters, and case-aggregation papers that place PSMF1 among autosomal recessive EOPD/parkinsonism genes.
